bullets.title: DELL blowout: AI servers $74B FY27 guide, $95B backlog, EPS +148%
bullets.body: Dell crushed F2Q27 with revenue $47.0B (+58% YoY), EPS $7.04 beating $4.91 consensus by 43%. AI server revenue hit $16.4B (+100% YoY) with $60.9B of orders in the quarter; FY27 guidance raised to $192B revenue and $25.50 EPS. Multiple houses raised PTs: Citi $600, JPM $635, Mizuho $600; only Deutsche Bank initiated at Hold ($480). Traditional servers also surged +122% YoY on enterprise modernization; supply remains the primary constraint.

bullets.title: AVGO F3Q26 beat; FY27 AI guide $115B, FY28 doubles to $230B — $30 EPS target
bullets.body: Broadcom posted AI semi revenue of $16.7B (+221% YoY) in F3Q26, guiding Q4 AI revenue to $21.7B (+236% YoY). Management raised FY27 AI revenue guidance from $100B to $115B and guided FY28 to double again to ~$230B, implying $30 EPS. Anthropic becomes largest XPU customer; OpenAI Jalapeño deploying 5GW+ in 2028. Citi raised PT to $515, JPM maintains OW at $580, UBS $470; stock was crowded long and pulled back ~5% after hours on slightly light Q4 guide vs buy-side.

bullets.title: SNOW +20%: third consecutive acceleration, AI driving half of upside; FY27 raised to 36%
bullets.body: Snowflake delivered F2Q27 product revenue of $1.49B (+37% YoY), beating by $68M, with Cortex Code at 9,100+ accounts and CoWork at 5,800. FY27 product revenue guidance raised to $6.07B (36% YoY). Q3 guidance implies 40%+ potential, ahead of all buy-side expectations. Citi upgraded to Buy ($490 PT from Neutral); KeyBanc raised PT to $460 OW; Wolfe raised PT to $500; UBS raised PT to $500.

bullets.title: NVDA: $13B Hugging Face deal, $3.5B MediaTek investment; renewed AI leadership
bullets.body: NVDA announced a $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face (one of its largest ever M&A deals) to control the leading open-source AI platform. Simultaneously, NVDA invested $3.5B in MediaTek convertible bonds to deepen the NVLink Fusion AI ecosystem. MS QDS data showed NVDA's up-capture vs the AI tech beneficiary basket tripled to 0.8x, the first AI semi leadership since 4Q24. GS sees NVDA at <10x CY28 EPS.

bullets.title: CIEN: FY27 30%+ revenue growth 'floor,' $10B+ backlog, supply constraints through 2028
bullets.body: Ciena beat F3Q26 (EPS $2.11 vs $1.73 est), raised FY26 guidance to $6.42B, and provided an early FY27 outlook: at least +30% revenue growth, GM 45-46%, OM 25-27%. Management characterized the 30% as a floor constrained by supply, not demand ceiling. Backlog exits FY26 at $10B+ with customer LTAs through 2029. JPM reiterated OW and raised Dec-27 PT to $605; Citi maintains $658 PT Buy; Wolfe raised to $660 OW; MS lowered to $425 EW citing GM uncertainty.

bullets.title: HPE raises FY27 guide to 13-17% growth; AI inferencing and Oracle deal as catalysts
bullets.body: HPE F3Q26 revenue $12.21B beat $11.97B consensus; EPS $1.11 vs $0.93 guide. Cloud & AI operating margin expanded to 17% from 7% YoY. FY27 revenue guidance raised to 13-17% from 8-12% on gigawatt-scale Oracle switching deal, AMD Helios opportunity, and $3.5B hyperscaler inferencing contract. FCF guidance raised to $5B+. Citi raised PT to $76 (Buy); JPM reiterates OW, PT $70. Stock fell -4-6% post-earnings on elevated expectations.

bullets.title: MDB: 30% growth, record Atlas net adds, EA at 36%—but stock -14% on 2H decel fears
bullets.body: MongoDB F2Q27 revenue $771.8M beat $735M (30.5% YoY), with Atlas at 28.9% YoY and record net new ARR of $127M. Enterprise Advanced grew 36% YoY. FY27 guidance raised $70M but implying 16% 2H growth vs 25% 1H, pressuring the stock. Q3 Atlas guided ~26% YoY vs buyside expectations of 30%+. Citi raised PT to $565 (Buy); Wolfe raised PT to $500 OW; Hedgeye is Long with +30% upside thesis; UBS trimmed to $410 Neutral.

bullets.title: ADBE: new CEO Anil Chakravarthy named; KeyBanc Underweight $195 PT, Citi Neutral $301
bullets.body: Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy (head of Digital Experience) as next CEO effective Dec 1, succeeding Shantanu Narayen who becomes executive chair. Stock initially fell 4% premarket. KeyBanc reiterated Underweight at $195 PT citing AI competition and decelerating organic ARR growth; Citi raised PT to $301 Neutral; Wolfe maintained Peer Perform noting strategic pivot toward data/enterprise from creativity roots. ADBE reports earnings Sep 10.

bullets.title: TTD: 15% workforce cut; Citi Sell at $11 PT on multi-quarter lag to durable growth
bullets.body: Trade Desk announced a ~15% RIF (~576 positions) expected to be completed in 3Q26, with $39M-$51M in restructuring charges. EBITDA margin guidance of 24.6% is 1,830bps below prior-year. Citi maintained Sell at $11 PT (5x '27 EV/EBITDA) citing continued advertiser headwinds and execution challenges. Stock was down ~15% in the week; several new products (Zuma, Measurement, Audience Unlimited) require multiple quarters before driving durable growth.

bullets.title: CRWD: Fal.Con 2026 — 20%+ FY28 NNARR guide, $10B/$20B ARR targets pulled forward 1 year
bullets.body: CrowdStrike's Fal.Con 2026 conference highlighted Guardian (AI agent security lifecycle) and SafeMind (frontier cybersecurity models). FY28 NNARR growth guidance of 20%+ was roughly double Street consensus of ~14%. $10B ARR target pulled forward to FY30 (from FY31), $20B to FY35 (from FY36). Citi maintained Buy ($260 PT); Roth raised PT to $220; Mizuho raised PT to $250 Outperform.

bullets.title: NFLX raises UK, Germany, Austria prices; ~2.5% firm-wide ARPU uplift expected
bullets.body: Netflix raised prices across UK, Germany, and Austria effective early September, affecting ~12% of total subscribers. Ad-tier increased 33-40% across markets; Standard/Premium up £1-2. Citi estimates ~2.5% firm-wide ARPU uplift though German/Austrian consumer protection laws may slow uptake. Citi maintains Buy at $100 PT (21% upside).

bullets.title: AAPL: iPhone 18 launch Sept 9; first foldable at $2,399+, Pro/Pro Max up $150-200
bullets.body: Apple's iPhone 18 launch event is scheduled for September 9 under new CEO John Ternus. The foldable iPhone Ultra starts at ~$2,399; Pro/Pro Max up $150-200 YoY due to 256GB memory cost inflation (+400% YoY). Total builds forecast 61.8M units for 2H26 including 7.5M foldable units. KeyBanc (Underweight, $250 PT) views the event as historically a modest negative catalyst. Citi and JPM constructive on premium mix and Services AI upside.

bullets.title: AFRM: FY27 GMV >$64B (+27% YoY); Scotiabank initiates Outperform at $95
bullets.body: Affirm guided FY27 GMV above $64B (+27% YoY), maintaining RLTC at ~4.2% of GMV. Q4 delivered ~30% GMV growth despite Prime Day timing shift and Walmart lapping. Key growth vectors include Affirm Card (80% interest-bearing attach), in-store adoption, and Affirm Edge launch in 2H FY27. Scotiabank initiated at sector outperform with $95 PT; JPM remains bullish with $29 PT.

bullets.title: HOOD: +18.6% on week after MS upgrade to OW ($150 PT); DKNG down on prediction market ruling
bullets.body: Robinhood surged 18.6% on the week driven by a Morgan Stanley upgrade to Overweight with $150 PT citing expanding platform economics, prediction market traction, and 23% revenue CAGR through 2028. Note: stock initially spiked on erroneous Blockworks crypto volume data which was later corrected to ~$2B from reported $36B. DKNG fell 3.8% after 9th Circuit ruled against Kalshi on sports prediction markets, creating circuit split uncertainty.

bullets.title: META upgraded to OW at Morgan Stanley ($775 PT); $17B legal settlement as clearing event
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley upgraded META to Overweight and top pick at $775 PT (bull case $1,000) following the $17B bipartisan AG settlement clearing regulatory overhang. The settlement enables new product launches (MetaClaw, Hatch, Watermelon model) and incremental $10+ EPS potential from AI agents. META trades at 16x forward EPS, ~25% below LT average. Separately, META launched Muse Spark 1.3 competitive with frontier AI models.

bullets.title: S&P index rebalances: ANET, DELL, SNDK, PANW added to S&P 100; BE, ILMN to S&P 500
bullets.body: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced the September 21 quarterly rebalance: Arista Networks, Dell, SanDisk, and Palo Alto Networks join the S&P 100; Bloom Energy and Illumina join the S&P 500; HubSpot and AGNC join the S&P MidCap 400. Changes effective prior to market open September 21, 2026 and represent passive flow tailwinds for newly included names.

bullets.title: UBER: 10% workforce cut (~3.3K employees); AI drives 70%+ of pull requests internally
bullets.body: Uber announced a ~10% global workforce reduction reducing management layers by 20% and cutting small/two-person teams by ~50%. Estimated gross annualized savings ~$825M. Company cited AI productivity gains (70%+ of code PRs now AI-driven, 52% cost reduction per session) as enabling the restructuring. Reinvestment targeted at AV programs and core growth. Citi maintained Buy; MS noted savings to fund Cybercab/AV initiatives.

bullets.title: CRM: Agentforce monetization shift to consumption; Wolfe upgrades to Outperform
bullets.body: Salesforce's product webinar showed Agentforce entering a consumption/outcome-based monetization phase with 10,000+ customers using at least one AI product and 50% of Q2 bookings from post-initial-credit top-ups. Agentforce pricing 60-80% above traditional seats; CRM Agentforce ARR hit $1.5B (+200% YoY). Wolfe upgraded to Outperform; MS and Citi incrementally more positive. The consensus view shifted to 'AI additive, not disruptive' for SaaS platforms.

bullets.title: TSLA Cybercab launches in Austin; MS sees progress but stock -4% post-event
bullets.body: Tesla officially launched Cybercab for public rides in Austin with 45 Cybercabs registered in Texas. The Morgan Stanley analyst maintained Overweight, viewing the event as an important rollout milestone with upcoming unsupervised fleet expansion serving as the next catalyst. Stock declined ~4% post-event on limited new disclosure. NHTSA opened an investigation into Cybercab self-certification.

bullets.title: CHTR CFO departs for Blackstone-Google AI infrastructure JV; no guidance change
bullets.body: Charter Communications CFO Jessica Fischer announced departure effective October 15, 2026 to join a newly formed Blackstone-Google AI infrastructure joint venture. Kevin Howard, EVP and Chief Accounting Officer, named interim CFO. Company reiterated all previously provided financial guidance. The departure signals risk around the ongoing Charter turnaround thesis per some sell-side analysts.
